details.description: GPT-4.1 nano is the smallest and fastest model in OpenAI's GPT-4.1 family, released April 14, 2025 for latency-sensitive tasks such as classification, autocompletion and information extraction. It takes text and image input and produces text-only output, keeps the family's 1-million-token context window despite its size, and has a knowledge cutoff of June 1, 2024. OpenAI's API deprecations page has since scheduled gpt-4.1-nano for shutdown on October 23, 2026, recommending gpt-5.6-luna as its replacement.
advantages: Scores 50.3% on GPQA Diamond and 29.4% on AIME 2024, both higher than GPT-4o mini's 40.2% and 8.6% on the same evaluations (OpenAI's GPT-4.1 announcement).
Scores 9.8% on Aider's polyglot coding benchmark (whole-file), roughly triple GPT-4o mini's 3.6% (OpenAI).
Keeps the GPT-4.1 family's 1-million-token context window despite being the smallest model in the line (OpenAI API model docs).
OpenAI describes it as the fastest and lowest-latency model in the GPT-4.1 family, built for quick, targeted tasks (OpenAI).
disadvantages: OpenAI's API deprecations page schedules gpt-4.1-nano for shutdown on October 23, 2026, with gpt-5.6-luna as the recommended replacement.
Scores 80.1% on MMLU, below GPT-4o mini's 82.0% on the same evaluation (OpenAI's GPT-4.1 announcement).
Output is text only; the model does not generate images, audio or video (OpenAI API model docs).
Knowledge cutoff of June 1, 2024 (OpenAI API model docs).
use_cases: High-volume, low-latency sub-tasks within a larger agent pipeline

sources.title: Introducing GPT-4.1 in the API | OpenAI

notes: IMPORTANT catalog discrepancy: the catalog's deprecation_date fact for this model is 2027-04-14, but OpenAI's own API deprecations page (section '2026-04-22: Legacy GPT model snapshots', fetched and grepped directly from the raw page HTML, not summarized) lists both the gpt-4.1-nano alias and the gpt-4.1-nano-2025-04-14 snapshot with shutdown date October 23, 2026 and recommended substitute gpt-5.6-luna -- over five months earlier than the catalog date. Flagging since it changes how current this model is. SWE-bench Verified was not reported for nano in OpenAI's comparison table (shown as '-'), so it is omitted from evaluations rather than guessed. OpenAI's GPT-4.1 launch post returned HTTP 403 to a direct fetch and was read via the r.jina.ai reader proxy instead; the cited URL is the original OpenAI page.
